laws.rule: In the Hohe Tauern National Park, visitors must stay on the trails, keep dogs on a lead throughout the park, and not make noise. Camping and making fires in open nature are not allowed; campsites in the national park municipalities can be used. Flowers, insects and minerals must be left where they are, and rubbish carried out. The park's page lists no fines and does not state drone or bicycle rules. The park covers parts of Salzburg, Tyrol and Carinthia, and this park-wide rule is held here once.
laws.heading: Was muss ich im Nationalpark beachten?, Nationalpark Hohe Tauern

laws.rule: Salzburg's overnight tax (allgemeine Nächtigungsabgabe) may not exceed EUR 1.95 per night in municipalities with no tourism association or a class C one (about A$3.10), or EUR 2.65 in class A or B municipalities (about A$4.21), at EUR 0.6293 per A$1 (RBA 30 Oct 2026). In spa districts (Kurbezirke) it must be between EUR 0.81 and EUR 3.68 (about A$1.29 to A$5.85). The limits are in sections 1 and 2 of the state ordinance in force since 1 December 2023, under section 5 of the Salzburger Nächtigungsabgabengesetz; each municipality sets its own rate within them.
laws.heading: Verordnung zu section 5 SNAG, paragraphs 1 and 2

laws.rule: Salzburg: without a supervising person, children may not be in public places from 21:00 to 05:00, young people to the end of their 14th year not from 23:00 to 05:00, and young people aged 14 to 16 not from 01:00 to 05:00. This does not apply on a timely way home (section 24(1) and (2) of the Salzburger Jugendgesetz). The same hours apply to other public events (section 33).
laws.heading: Salzburger Jugendgesetz, sections 24 and 33

laws.rule: Salzburg: up to the end of the 16th year, buying, having and drinking alcohol is banned. From 16, spirits (above 0.5% alcohol, also in mixed drinks such as alcopops) are banned, and other alcohol may be drunk only if it does not obviously cause drunkenness. Children and young people may not buy, have or use tobacco products, and none may be sold to them (section 36(1) and (2) of the Salzburger Jugendgesetz).
laws.heading: Salzburger Jugendgesetz, section 36

laws.rule: In Salzburg the mayor can ban camping (tents, motorhomes, caravans) outside campsites where safety, health, the local community, farming, tourism, nature or the landscape would be badly harmed, and a council can by regulation allow it only at set places or ban it at set places (section 13 of the Salzburger Campingplatzgesetz). Ask the council for the local regulation. The fine scale was not read.

items.text: Salzburg's youth-protection law (Jugendgesetz, section 36): under 16, no alcohol; from 16 to 18, no spirits of more than 0.5% alcohol by volume, even when mixed, and other alcohol only if it is not obviously causing intoxication. The ban includes powder and paste carriers. Offences against section 36 that are not committed in public are not punished. In this law a child is under 12, and Jugendliche are 12 to 18, except a person serving in the Bundesheer or Zivildienst. Fines: a young person up to EUR 220 (about A$350); an adult EUR 250 to EUR 3,700 (about A$397 to A$5,880).

psychoactive-substances.notes: These are Land youth-protection rules, not a general adult drinking age of 18 for beer or wine. They apply to visitors under 18 in this Land. Federal narcotics law is not restated here. AUD at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293. Official RIS consolidated text (Geltende Fassung) read directly on 11 November 2026.
